# Themes

<Lead>
A theme sets the whole look: color, type, corners and labels. Each theme has a light and a dark color scheme. Components never need to know which one is active.
</Lead>

| Theme | Look |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | Calm and neutral, for tools people use all day. Inter, rounded corners, blue accents. |
| `ledger` | Crisp and dense, drawn the way Blueprint draws it. IBM Plex, 2 to 3px corners, Blueprint's grays and elevation, violet accents. |

`styles.css` includes the default theme. Every other theme ships its own stylesheet.

## Use a theme

Load the theme's stylesheet after the main one. `fonts.css` is optional and loads every theme's typefaces. Browsers download only the ones a page uses.

```tsx
import "@clawscale/react/styles.css";
import "@clawscale/react/themes/ledger.css";
import "@clawscale/react/fonts.css";
```

Pick it on the provider, and pass the same default to `ThemeScript` so the first paint matches.

```tsx
<ClawscaleProvider defaultTheme="ledger">{children}</ClawscaleProvider>
```

```tsx
<ThemeScript defaultTheme="ledger" />
```

Without its stylesheet, a theme falls back to the default look, and the provider logs a warning.

## Let people choose

`useTheme` returns the theme and a setter. The choice is saved, like the color scheme. `themes` from `@clawscale/tokens` holds every built-in theme with its `label` and `description`, so a dropdown can list them all. This one changes the theme of these docs. So does Shift + T.

<Example name="guides/themes/picker">
  <ThemesPicker />
</Example>

## Accents

An accent sets the primary color: buttons, links, focus rings, selection and selected rows. Every other color stays with the theme. Each theme lists its accents, its own first.

| Theme | Accents |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | Blue, violet, teal |
| `ledger` | Violet, blue, teal |

`setAccent` changes the accent and saves it, like the theme. A saved accent that the active theme lacks falls back to the theme's own. `themeAccents(theme)` from `@clawscale/tokens` lists a theme's accents with their colors. This picker changes the accent of these docs.

<Example name="guides/themes/accent-picker">
  <ThemesAccentPicker />
</Example>

To start with an accent, pass `defaultAccent` to the provider and to `ThemeScript`.

```tsx
<ClawscaleProvider defaultTheme="ledger" defaultAccent="teal">{children}</ClawscaleProvider>
```

## Themes and color schemes

The theme and the color scheme are separate settings. `colorScheme` picks light, dark or system for any theme. See [Clawscale provider](/docs/core/clawscale-provider/).

| Attribute on `<html>` | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `data-cs-theme` | `default`, `ledger` or the name of your own theme |
| `data-cs-accent` | An accent of that theme, or absent for the theme's own |
| `data-cs-color-scheme` | `light` or `dark` |

## Scope a theme

Set `data-cs-theme` on any element to give its subtree another theme, and `data-cs-color-scheme` for another color scheme. Both nest, and the closest one wins.

```tsx
<Card data-cs-theme="ledger">...</Card>
```

An accent applies where `data-cs-accent` sits on the same element as `data-cs-theme`, as the provider sets both on `<html>`.

```tsx
<Card data-cs-theme="ledger" data-cs-accent="teal">...</Card>
```

Overlays render in a portal on `<body>`, so they take the page's theme. Inside a scoped subtree, render them in place with `usePortal={false}`.

## Browser support

A theme's own rules sit inside `@scope`, and can use `corner-shape` and `light-dark()`.

- Browsers without `corner-shape` keep rounded corners.
- Browsers without `@scope` get the theme's tokens: its colors, fonts, corners and labels. They skip its own rules.

## Build your own theme

A theme is data: a `ThemeDefinition` from `@clawscale/tokens` with shared tokens, a light and a dark color scheme and a sequential ramp. Start from a built-in theme, render its CSS with `renderThemeCss` and load the file after the Clawscale styles.

```ts
import { blue, renderThemeCss, type ThemeDefinition, themes, withAccent } from "@clawscale/tokens";

// The default theme with teal as its own accent, and blue to pick.
const base = withAccent(themes.default, "teal");

export const harbor: ThemeDefinition = {
  ...base,
  name: "harbor",
  label: "Harbor",
  description: "The default theme with teal accents.",
  accent: { name: "teal", label: "Teal" },
  accents: [blue],
};

// At build time, write the CSS and load it after @clawscale/react/styles.css.
const css = renderThemeCss(harbor);
```

Then pass `defaultTheme="harbor"`. Check every text and intent color with `contrastRatio` from `@clawscale/tokens`, as Clawscale's own tests do.
